# fix(codex-mcp-guard): clear all 6 npm advisories via lockfile-only bump

<!-- Generated by SessionEnd hook from a commit matching a journal-worthy pattern.
     Next session: review, then promote to a real journal entry OR delete. -->

**Commit**: `941cd1409a3c` — fix(codex-mcp-guard): clear all 6 npm advisories via lockfile-only bump

**Body**:

Closes the HIGH hono CORS advisory (#43) and five siblings the issue did not
enumerate. `npm audit` went from 6 vulnerabilities (1 low, 3 moderate, 2 high)
to 0.

hono 4.12.18 -> 4.12.33, above the vulnerable <=4.12.26 range. The issue named
one advisory (GHSA-88fw-hqm2-52qc, CORS reflects any Origin with credentials);
that version range actually carried 10+, plus fast-uri (HIGH host confusion),
@hono/node-server, body-parser and qs.

@modelcontextprotocol/sdk 1.29.0 -> 1.30.0, which is what pulls hono in
transitively. That is inside the declared ^1.29.0 caret, so it is non-breaking
by semver and package.json is untouched — lockfile-only, matching the issue's
remediation ("bump at the template source so consumers receive the fix on the
next /sync").

Verified: npm ci from the new lockfile succeeds; `node server.js --self-check`
exits 0 with POLICIES_POPULATED=true and all three tool lanes resolving their
hook sets.

NOT fixed here, and NOT introduced here: `npm test` reports 2 pre-existing
failures in the degraded-mode lane ("apply_patch degraded: expected DENY, got
allow=true" and the git-mut sibling). Reproduced identically against the OLD
lockfile before the bump, so they are independent of this change. They appear
related to today's sync of signing-mutation-guard.js; filed separately rather
than bundled into a dependency bump.
